answers: A 12-year-old was killed and two other boys were injured after a chain link fence electrified by a live underground wire electrocuted them at a city park in Georgia. During football practice at Fleming park in Augusta on Monday, Melquan Robinson hopped a fence to retrieve a ball, WRDW reports, citing the incident report that says when he "went to come back over the fence, he was electrocuted." The seventh-grader was pronounced dead later at Children's Hospital of Georgia, according to the Augusta Chronicle. Two other boys who tried to help their friend were injured and hospitalized, according to reports. The mother of one of them, David Sette, tells WRDW that her son is improving. Per the Chronicle, an adult also was injured in the incident. "We lost a future leader. We lost a future athlete. We lost a child in our city," Melquan's former coach, acting as a spokesman for the bereaved family, tells the Chronicle. The oldest of three children, Melquan loved his family and was very protective of his siblings, he says. Multiple investigations into the incident are reportedly underway, with city officials looking into how the fence became electrified. Georgia Power, offering "condolences and sympathy," said in a statement that the utility "does not control or maintain the voltage" that caused the electrocution. Melquan's family will hold a vigil Thursday at the Bernie Ward Community Center. "This young man was where he needed to be," his former coach says, per WRDW. "He was doing what he loved." (A medieval re-enactor was impaled in a freak accident.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passages:**

On Monday, a tragic incident occurred at the Fleming Athletic Complex near the Bernie Ward Community Center in Augusta, Georgia, when a 12-year-old boy, Melquan Kwame Robinson, was electrocuted after touching a live wire that had come into contact with a chain-link fence. The incident happened during football practice at the Lumpkin Road complex. Melquan, a seventh-grader at Morgan Road Middle School, was attempting to retrieve a football that had gone over the fence. As he climbed back over, he was electrocuted and later pronounced dead at 9:56 p.m. at the Children's Hospital of Georgia.

Three other individuals were injured in the incident, including two juveniles and one adult. Two of the injured were Melquan’s friends who attempted to pull him from the fence and were also shocked. Their conditions were not immediately available, but one of the boys was moved from ICU to a regular hospital room. The family of one of the injured boys expressed concern over potential long-term effects from muscle breakdown caused by the electrocution.

Melquan’s former football coach, Don Clark, described the boy as energetic, athletic, and passionate about sports. He emphasized the emotional impact of the tragedy on the community, noting that Melquan was a future leader and athlete. Clark also highlighted the bravery of the two friends who tried to save Melquan, calling their actions "heartbreaking" and "inspiring."

The city of Augusta, which owns and operates the community center and athletic complex, has launched an investigation into how the live wire came into contact with the fence. The Georgia Power company stated that it does not control or maintain the voltage that energized the fence, and it will cooperate with local officials during the investigation.

The incident has led to the cancellation of all football activities at Fleming Park for the rest of the week. A vigil is planned for Thursday at 6 p.m. at the Bernie Ward Community Center, open to the entire community. The city’s mayor and local officials have expressed their condolences and support for the Robinson family and the affected individuals.

The tragedy has left the community in shock, with many expressing grief over the loss of a young life and the impact on families, friends, and teammates. The incident serves as a reminder of the importance of safety measures at public facilities and the need for community solidarity during times of loss.
